<jats:title>A<jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>
                     </jats:title><jats:p>Two-dimensional SU(<jats:italic>N</jats:italic>) gauge theory coupled to a Majorana fermion in the adjoint representation is a nice toy model for higher-dimensional gauge dynamics. It possesses a multitude of “gluinoball” bound states whose spectrum has been studied using numerical diagonalizations of the light-cone Hamiltonian. We extend this model by coupling it to <jats:italic>N</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>f</jats:italic></jats:sub> flavors of fundamental Dirac fermions (quarks). The extended model also contains meson-like bound states, both bosonic and fermionic, which in the large-<jats:italic>N</jats:italic> limit decouple from the gluinoballs. We study the large-<jats:italic>N</jats:italic> meson spectrum using the Discretized Light-Cone Quantization (DLCQ). When all the fermions are massless, we exhibit an exact <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$ \mathfrak{osp} $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>osp</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>(1|4) symmetry algebra that leads to an infinite number of degeneracies in the DLCQ approach. More generally, we show that many single-trace states in the theory are threshold bound states that are degenerate with multi-trace states. These exact degeneracies can be explained using the Kac-Moody algebra of the SU(<jats:italic>N</jats:italic>) current. We also present strong numerical evidence that additional threshold states appear in the continuum limit. Finally, we make the quarks massive while keeping the adjoint fermion massless. In this case too, we observe some exact degeneracies that show that the spectrum of mesons becomes continuous above a certain threshold. This demonstrates quantitatively that the fundamental string tension vanishes in the massless adjoint QCD<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> without explicit four-fermion operators.</jats:p>
title: Exact symmetries and threshold states in two-dimensional models for QCD
